subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Which provider-family fallback contract should OpenClaw expose for this issue: wildcard/auto refs, explicit grouped fallback families, catalog-derived fallback candidates, or no new core config surface?
rationale: The remaining work changes a public model/provider fallback and config contract, and the current evidence shows several plausible but incompatible shapes with different upgrade and operator-cost implications.

options.title: Choose one core fallback contract
options.body: Pick a single schema/runtime shape and require implementation across config, fallback resolution, embedded-run gates, docs, and migration/doctor behavior before landing.

options.title: Defer to existing explicit fallbacks
options.body: Keep `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` as the only core fallback contract and close or redirect wildcard/grouped proposals once maintainers confirm that direction.

options.title: Route only dynamic policy to plugins
options.body: Use plugin hooks for pre-run model routing while keeping post-failure provider-family fallback semantics out of core unless a missing plugin API is identified.

recommendation.title: Choose one core fallback contract
recommendation.body: Pick a single schema/runtime shape and require implementation across config, fallback resolution, embedded-run gates, docs, and migration/doctor behavior before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The central fallback behavior appears to date to Peter Steinberger's model fallback refactors, and he has the strongest sampled ownership signal for the affected code path.
